question: How should the segmented control's glass thumb move when you pick another option?
context: Every segmented control (View | Edit in the title bar, the panel's pickers) now has a lighter glass thumb that stretches across and settles when the pick changes. Try it in Photonz Dev once it refreshes, then pick.

options.label: Keep it as it is
options.summary: Picking an option stretches the glass over both options, squashes it a touch, then it lets go and settles a few points past its new place. About four tenths of a second.
pros: Reads as liquid glass, which is what you asked for
cons: On a fast run of clicks it can feel a little slow
options.mitigation: A second click mid-move carries on from where the glass is, so it never waits.

options.label: Quicker, same shape
options.summary: The same stretch and settle, in about a quarter of a second.
cons: The stretch is harder to see at that speed
options.mitigation: The squash can be made a little deeper so it still reads.

options.label: A plain glide
options.summary: No stretch or squash: the glass slides across and eases to a stop, like the system control.
pros: Never distracting in a dense panel
cons: Loses the liquid feel you asked for
options.mitigation: The glass itself still refracts as it moves, so it is not flat paint.

withdrawn.reason: Overtaken: the user answered it themselves on 2026-09-29 ('overshoots like CRAZY... doesn't feel mac native'). The stretch-and-settle it asks about is gone; a new card asks about the glide that replaced it.
